storeWriteMs.margin: Shared-runner allowance; median of five full 10,000-row normalizations.

storeReadMs.margin: Shared-runner allowance; median of five 10,000-fragment traversals.

storeCollectMs.margin: Shared-runner allowance; median of five full unretained collections.

storeHeapBytes.margin: Retained normalized graph after forced GC; excludes the preallocated input.

storeAfterGCBytes.margin: Allows V8 bookkeeping noise while catching retention of the full graph.

burstMs.margin: 100 events over one simulated second; median of five wall-time runs on shared runners. Measured again 2026-11-13 after incremental reads; it was 32.552.

burstNotifications.margin: Exactly one per changed row, no notification amplification; also asserted equal to 100.

eventMs1000.margin: Milliseconds for one event changing one row of a 1,000-row list with 1,000 fragment subscribers; mean of 100 events, median of five runs. It was 1.6 before incremental reads, so the limit catches a return to reading the whole list, with room for a runner several times slower.

eventMs10000.margin: The same with 10,000 rows. It was 25 before incremental reads. What remains grows with the list: one memo lookup per row, and one check per subscriber.

compileMs.margin: About seven times the local median, for shared CI runners. Was 30000: tightened after a nested compile re-extended the whole schema per live type, which took this from 7.6 s to about 24 s and stayed under the old limit.

mainRawBytes.margin: Minified standalone entry closure, external peers; streams and readAll have their own entries. Measured size plus about 1,000. Raised 2026-11-17 for write-outcome evidence (#60, #61, #62: mostly the validation rule names the router sends as codes), to 69821, for stopping live delivery on an authentication close and resuming it (#73), to 71869, for query reads (#63, #66, #67, #72: deadlines, retry, missing-field reports, refetch by variables), to 76437, and for several @connection lists per query, restarting a list on a refused cursor and batched refetchFragment (#83, #55, #82), to 84561. Growth past this needs a reason.

mainGzipBytes.margin: Gzip of the same closure, plus about 300. Raised with the raw limit on 2026-11-17, four times (22574, 23101, 24705, then 27168).

reactRawBytes.margin: Standalone React closure including shared client code; peers external. The measurement of 6969 was stale by 2026-11-17 (9317 on main, from useFragmentList and the hooks added since); re-measured at 9986 with useSuspenseLoadedQuery (#102), and the limit raised from 10000 to that plus about 1,000.

reactGzipBytes.margin: Level-9 gzip of the React closure. Re-measured at 3907 with useSuspenseLoadedQuery (#102), and raised from 4000 to that plus about 300.

inspectorRawBytes.margin: Standalone development inspector closure (graphql-orm-client/inspector), with the store reader it shares with main. Measured size plus about 1,000. Added 2026-11-17 (#104); main is unchanged by it.

inspectorGzipBytes.margin: Level-9 gzip of the inspector closure, plus about 300.

windows1HeapBytes.margin: 10,000 rows per real window; permits browser/V8 version variance.

windows1Sockets.margin: Exactly one socket per window; also checked during readiness.

windowMarginalHeapBytes.margin: Maximum marginal JS heap across 1→3 and 3→6 windows; browser variance allowance.

baselineMethod: Median of five complete command runs; each timing within each command is itself a median of five samples. Window heap is a median of five independent browser runs.
